key_insight: PseudoBench shows that agentic auto-research systems can convincingly amplify pseudoscience instead of rejecting it, with near-zero refusal and weak resistance overall.
engineering_relevance: For AI research agents, scientific alignment and guardrails are needed before deployment to prevent plausible but misleading outputs from contaminating research workflows.
method: Built PseudoBench with 200 curated pseudoscientific claim–evidence pairs across five domains.
Evaluated agents end-to-end through an autonomous research pipeline, from experimentation to writing.
Tested seven state-of-the-art agentic systems on their ability to identify and resist pseudoscientific narratives.
evidence_signal: Across seven agents, refusal was near zero and the highest measured resistance was only 27.4%, while stronger agents tended to produce more sophisticated, more credible-looking pseudoscientific reports.
watch_item: The benchmark focuses on curated adversarial cases, so real-world performance may vary outside these controlled pseudoscientific narratives.
paper_title: PseudoBench: Measuring How Agentic Auto-Research Fuels Pseudoscience
